data.title: Libya reopens oil pipeline to Zawiya
data.description:
An oil pipeline from Libya's Hamada and Tahara oilfields to Zawiya was reopened on Saturday, according to the head of the state-owned oil firm National Oil Corporation.

A pipeline valve was closed by individuals who entered the crude oil receiving station near the Zawiya refinery on Thursday, leading to a reduction in production at both fields.

data.title: India's basmati rice yield likely to be 5-10% higher this year: Industry leader
data.description:
India's basmati rice yield is expected to increase by 5 to 10 per cent this year compared to the previous year, supported by favourable rainfall and better crop conditions, according to Rajeev Setia, President, Basmati IREF, and Joint Managing Director, Chaman Lal Setia Exports Ltd.

Speaking to ANI on the sidelines of the Bharat International Rice Conference 2026 in New Delhi, Setia said the monsoon and subsequent rainfall had supported the growth of the basmati crop, resulting in expectations of higher yields.

"The monsoon was reasonable... and thereafter there were good rains. Just look around, greenery we have all around. So in that way the crop grew and the yield in this particular year for basmati rice is higher," he said.

Asked about the expected increase, Setia said, "It will definitely be 5-10%... higher as compared to the preceding year." The expected improvement in yields is significant for India's basmati rice industry, as higher agricultural productivity could support export availability amid expectations of growing international demand.

Setia also expressed optimism about the long-term demand for Indian basmati rice, pointing to the increasing popularity of Indian food across international markets. "The requirement of Basmati is likely to grow in the time to come," he told ANI. He said Indian basmati rice has established a presence across international markets, while his own company exports to 96 countries.

Setia noted that the growing popularity of Indian cuisine among consumers in Europe and the United States is helping expand the market for basmati rice beyond traditional consumers. He also highlighted India's position in the global basmati rice trade, noting that the crop has geographical indication (GI) recognition and is cultivated in specific geographical regions.

India is one of the world's leading producers and exporters of basmati rice, with the crop playing an important role in the country's agricultural exports. Higher yields could improve supply availability, although actual export performance will also depend on international demand and market conditions.

The Bharat International Rice Conference 2026 is being held from October 23 to 25 in New Delhi, bringing together Indian exporters, international buyers and other stakeholders in the global rice trade.

data.title: China's Communist Party names new provincial chiefs ahead of fifth plenum
data.description:
By Eduardo Baptista

China's ruling Communist Party announced key personnel changes in six provinces on Saturday, including two new provincial party chiefs and six officials positioned to become governors, before it holds a closed-door conclave in Beijing from October 26 to 29.

The official focus of the secretive meeting, also known as a plenum, in the Chinese capital is expected to be party governance and discipline, though personnel issues could also feature.

Here are the appointments:

  • State Council Vice Secretary-General Wang Zhijun was named Communist Party secretary of the southern province of Hunan, replacing Shen Xiaoming

  • Wang is a full member of the Central Committee, the ​largest of the party's top decision-making bodies

  • Mo Gaoyi, a vice minister at the party's publicity department and director of the State Council Information Office, was named party secretary of the southwestern province of Yunnan, replacing Wang Ning

  • Xie Weijiang, Hunan's deputy party secretary and party chief of Yueyang, a city in the province's northeast, was named secretary of the provincial government's party group, signalling he is set to succeed Governor Mao Weiming

  • Guo Ningning, Fujian's deputy party secretary and party chief of the provincial capital Fuzhou, was named secretary of the provincial government's party group, signalling she is set to become governor

  • Lin Tao was named Fujian deputy party secretary, while Qin Haixiang replaced Guo as Fuzhou party chief

  • Zhuge Yujie, previously deputy party secretary of central Hubei province, was named deputy party secretary of the northwestern province of Qinghai and secretary of its provincial government's party group, signalling he is set to become governor

  • Chen Yongqi, southern Jiangxi's deputy party secretary and head of its political and legal affairs commission, was named secretary of the provincial government's party group, signalling he is set to become governor. His predecessor, Ye Jianchun, was placed under investigation in August for alleged disciplinary violations

  • Zhao Chenxin was named deputy party secretary of the northern province of Hebei and secretary of the provincial government's party group, signalling he is set to succeed Governor Wang Zhengpu

  • Liu Qifan, previously deputy party secretary of Qinghai, was named deputy party secretary of Yunnan and secretary of the provincial government's party group, signalling he is set to succeed Governor Wang Yubo

  • Provincial legislatures must formally elect the gubernatorial appointments, but that is generally a procedural step after the party's decision

data.title: JST Buyback & Burn Upgrade: GasFree Revenue and $20.34M Surplus Injected as JUST’s Ecosystem Trio Solidifies JST Token Value
data.description:
Summary:

The upgraded JST Buyback and Burn program features the following highlights:

  • $50M Treasury Reserve Cushion: Establishes a safety buffer for sustainable ecosystem operations.
  • Expanded Funding Sources: Integrates GasFree revenue alongside JustLend and USDD to cover 100% of JUST core products.
  • ~$20.34M Capital Injection: Unlocks legacy surplus funds to be released in phases for future buybacks.
  • JUST DAO Execution: Complete on-chain execution with full transparency and open-source verification.

Following its recent brand refresh on October 23, JUST—the flagship on-chain DeFi infrastructure on TRON—officially unveiled its upgraded JST Buyback & Burn initiative that strengthens the value-accrual framework of the native governance token. Building on previous funding sources from JustLend and USDD, the upgraded mechanism incorporates business revenue from GasFree while allocating $20.34 million in capital surplus to future token repurchases. These changes diversify the protocol’s revenue base and set a structured process for deploying surplus capital.

The updated framework expands JST buyback funding from a dual-revenue stream (i.e., JustLend and USDD) to a more robust three-pillar model (i.e., JustLend, USDD, and GasFree), reinforced by phased injections of existing funds. Beyond simply adding capital, this upgrade ensures that growth in each JUST product line directly accrues to JST’s underlying value. It underscores JUST’s long-term commitment to token value accrual while tightly aligning protocol incentives with JST holders and the broader community.

JST Buyback & Burn Upgraded: $50M Safety Cushion, GasFree Revenue Integration, and $20.34M Surplus Injection

As the native governance token of the JUST ecosystem, JST’s underlying value support and utility mechanisms have always been a central focus for the community. With the successful completion of the 5th buyback and burn on October 16, Phase 1 of the JST Buyback and Burn program concluded smoothly, paving the way for the upgraded mechanism alongside JUST’s broader brand refresh.

According to the Announcement: Upgrade to the JST Buyback & Burn Mechanism, the newly updated framework outlines key structural arrangements across five core areas, establishing clear risk boundaries while securing a more stable and predictable capital foundation for future buybacks:

  • $50M Treasury Safety Floor: A baseline reserve of at least $50 million will be maintained long-term to manage risk scenarios, guarantee liquidity, and ensure protocol solvency under extreme market conditions.
  • More Diversified Funding Sources: The upgraded model integrates GasFree revenue alongside existing JustLend and USDD streams, extending buyback capital across all three core JUST product lines. Specific sources now include revenue from JustLend’s sTRX staking and SBM, GasFree income, and the USDD protocol revenue exceeding the $10 million threshold.
  • Structured Surplus Capital Deployment: All protocol funds above the $50 million treasury reserve floor are dedicated entirely to JST buybacks. An initial $20.34 million—sourced from cumulative GasFree earnings and surplus treasury reserves above the safety floor—has been unlocked, and will be deployed across four buyback rounds starting in Q4 2026.
  • Buyback & Burn Execution: The protocol is adopting a “continuous buyback, periodic burn” approach. Funded by 100% of revenue across all product lines, open-market buybacks will adjust dynamically to prevailing market depth and liquidity, with accumulated tokens burned on a regular schedule.
  • On-Chain Governance: All buybacks and burns will be executed by JUST DAO. Key financial figures will be disclosed to the community on a regular basis, and every transaction will remain fully verifiable on-chain. 

Compared to Phase 1, this upgrade introduces three structural shifts:

  • Clearer capital boundaries. The $50 million reserve floor creates a solvency backstop while defining the boundaries of capital eligible for buybacks. 
  • More diversified funding sources. Rather than relying primarily on JustLend and USDD, integrating GasFree extends revenue capture across the entire JUST ecosystem. Meanwhile, deploying roughly $20.34 million in surplus funds across future tranches smooths buyback execution and ensures an orderly transition between mechanism phases. 
  • Streamlined execution under unified governance. By adopting a “continuous buyback, periodic burn” strategy, the consolidated JUST DAO (formerly JustLend DAO) takes full operational ownership of buybacks and burns. This aligns governance and execution under a single authority, matching JUST’s brand consolidation and holistic governance roadmap. 

In essence, the updated mechanism follows a clear tripartite playbook: secure the downside, deploy surplus capital, and compound with organic growth. It first anchors ecosystem stability with the $50 million reserve floor, primes buyback momentum by releasing roughly $20.34 million in surplus funds, and then hands the baton to ongoing revenues from all three verticals—turning JST buybacks into a sustainable, business-backed deflationary engine.

GasFree Poised to Become the Second Growth Engine for JST Buybacks After JustLend

The integration of GasFree revenue represents the key highlight of this mechanism upgrade. Scheduled to begin capital allocations in Q4 2026, GasFree has demonstrated strong cash-flow generation and is positioned to become the second growth engine for JST buyback funding after JustLend.

Built on TRON, GasFree is a native gasless solution that lets users pay transaction fees directly with the tokens they transfer, removing the friction of holding TRX or other native tokens just to move funds. By enabling single-asset fee settlement, GasFree eliminates one of the most stubborn usability hurdles in on-chain transfers. The service currently supports gasless transfers for both USDT and USDD.

Operationally, GasFree’s user base and network activity continue to climb at a rapid pace. As of October 23, GasFree has processed over $157.1 billion in cumulative stablecoin transfer volume across more than 9.14 million transactions, serving an aggregate user base exceeding 500,000 unique addresses. This surging operational momentum provides the solid backing for GasFree to consistently fuel the buyback pool and establish itself as JST’s second major growth engine.

From a revenue standpoint, GasFree’s profitability is backed by hard data. It has proven to be a vital growth engine since its March 2025 rollout, generating approximately $12.03 million in cumulative revenue through Q3 2026. This performance underpinned the recent extraction of roughly $20.34 million in surplus funds, sourced directly from GasFree’s accrued earnings and surplus treasury holdings above the reserve floor.

As GasFree’s financial contribution accelerates, JST’s buyback-and-burn model enters a new stage of multi-business synergy. The token’s value-accrual mechanism is now deeply tied to the growth of the broader JUST ecosystem and fully synchronized with the protocol’s multi-product expansion.

Diversified Value Accrual: JUST’s Core Products Unite to Back JST

Under the updated mechanism, GasFree revenue is now directly allocated to JST buybacks, alongside qualifying net revenue from USDD. This marks a pivotal evolution: JST burns no longer rely solely on JustLend. Instead, they are fueled by a diversified, multi-product revenue base spanning JustLend, USDD, and GasFree.

This multi-pronged funding approach mirrors the broader JUST rebrand. Moving forward, JustLend, USDD, and GasFree unite under a single brand and user gateway—with JUST DAO steering cross-product governance, ecosystem synergy, and sustainable tokenomics for JST.

JST serves as the native governance token for the entire JUST ecosystem. Through this unified rebrand and the rollout of JUST DAO governance, JST’s value foundation now spans the protocol’s core utility layers: lending and resource markets via JustLend, decentralized stablecoin infrastructure via USDD, and gasless transfer settlement via GasFree. JST is no longer anchored to a single product line; its value capture is directly tied to the growth of the entire ecosystem.

As a pillar of TRON’s financial infrastructure, JUST commands roughly $12.2 billion in Total Value Locked (TVL)—consistently securing nearly half of the network’s total liquidity, with all three business pillars holding leading positions in their respective verticals.

Among them, JustLend remains foundational: having fully funded the initial phase of JST buybacks and burns, it now provides the core yield baseline under the upgraded mechanism. As of October 23, JustLend’s TVL surpassed $7.13 billion, with its supply-borrow market (SBM) driving approximately $3.71 billion, cementing its status as a global DeFi lending leader. In the staking sector, total TRX staked has crossed 9.83 billion. At the same time, through sTRX-powered Energy solutions, JustLend has become a primary Energy gateway for the TRON network, scaling both on-demand Energy purchases and long-term rental services.

Meanwhile, GasFree continues to scale as a key revenue driver. In late September, GasFree partnered with Binance Web3 Wallet to introduce TRC-20 USDT gas fee delegation. Users can now pay network fees directly in USDT without needing to hold TRX. Securing integration with a Tier-1 wallet validates GasFree’s business model and significantly expands its addressable market and fee-generation capacity.

data.title: EPS-95 pension: Bombay High Court rules in favour of private sector employees seeking pension on higher wages
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 24 -- Private sector employees seeking a higher pension under the Employees' Pension Scheme (EPS), 1995, have received relief from the Bombay High Court.

The court has ruled that the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) cannot reject an employee's application for a higher pension merely because the employer's provident fund (PF) trust rules cap contributions at the statutory wage ceiling or do not expressly allow higher pension contributions.

In its October 19, 2026, judgment, Justice Sandeep V. Marne set aside EPFO orders rejecting applications filed by over 40 private-sector employees of establishments including Abbott India, Tata Communications, Raymond Steel and BEST Undertaking.

The court directed EPFO to process and allow the petitioners' joint-option applications within eight weeks.

Employees and employers make contributions towards the employee's provident fund, while a portion of the employer's contribution is ordinarily diverted to the EPS, subject to the scheme's rules.

The statutory wage ceiling is the salary limit used to calculate contributions under the applicable rules. The EPS ceiling was raised to Rs.15,000 a month in 2014 (further raised to Rs.25,000 from 17 September 2026).

However, eligible employees who had contributed to their PF on actual salaries above the statutory ceiling can seek a higher pension by opting to calculate pension contributions on higher wages, subject to the scheme's conditions.

This is where the joint option comes in. It is an option exercised jointly by the employee and employer to seek pension based on higher wages instead of being restricted to the statutory ceiling.

"The common issue of law which is involved in these Petitions is whether private trust rules of a provident fund trust of an exempted establishment under the Employees' Provided Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 (EPF Act) can govern the contribution to the Employees' Pension Fund of employers or restrict the exercise of Joint Option under paragraph 11(3) /11 (4) of Employees Pension Scheme,1995 (EPS, 1995)," according to the ruling document.

For example, if an employee's salary was Rs.40,000 a month and PF contributions were made on that actual salary, the employee may seek a higher pension based on higher wages, subject to eligibility and the required contributions.

Some employers had their own PF trusts because their establishments were exempted from the usual EPF arrangement. The trusts' internal rules restricted contributions to the statutory wage ceiling or did not expressly provide for higher pension contributions.

EPFO relied on these rules to reject the employees' joint-option applications. In some cases, it also cited missing documents or questions about contributions on eligible salary components.

The employees challenged these decisions, arguing that internal PF trust rules could not override the statutory EPS provisions.

Justice Sandeep V. Marne noted that "I have heard Mr. Surana, the learned counsel appearing for the Petitioners, who submits that the issue is conclusively answered by the judgment of the Apex Court in Sunil Kumar B. (supra), which holds that an exempted and unexempted establishments stand on par."

"He submits that the Trust Rules operate only in the field of provident fund and that the same has no bearing on employee's entitlement for pension on higher wages."

"Per contra, Ms. Gandhi, the learned counsel appearing for the Respondent-EPFO submits that the Applications of the Petitioners are rightly rejected by the Competent Authority after duly applying its mind to the entire material on record," Marne added.

Several High Courts had ruled that PF trust rules could not, by themselves, be used to deny eligible employees the benefit of a higher pension under the EPS. The Bombay High Court held that the rules governing an employer's PF trust could not be used as the sole ground to reject an otherwise eligible employee's joint option.

Marne said, "In my view, therefore all the Petitions deserve to be allowed. As consistently held by various High Courts, the rules/deeds of provident fund trusts of an exempted establishment operate only in respect of the provident fund, unless an exemption under Section 17(1)(c) of the EPF Act read with paragraph 39 of the EPS, 1995, including joint option, applies to the employees in same manner as the employees of unexempted establishments."

"A joint option cannot be rejected on the ground that the Trust Rules either envisage a cap /ceiling or employer's contribution or that Trust Rules did not provide for joint option on higher pension on the ground that employer did not remit pension contribution on the wages exceeding the ceiling," he added.

The court also addressed cases where employers could not produce old records. Referring to earlier judgments, it noted that alternative verification methods, including giving employees an opportunity to be heard, should be considered where records are unavailable.

The EPFO had also argued that contributions on certain salary components needed verification. However, the court found no reason to distinguish the Tata Communications case on the grounds presented, as the central reason for rejection remained the restrictions in the trust rules.

The court set aside the EPFO orders rejecting the applications and directed the authorities to process and allow the petitioners' joint options for higher pension within eight weeks. The petitions were allowed, with no order as to costs.

"Impugned orders passed by the EPFO rejecting applications filed by the Petitioners for availing benefit of pension on higher wages under paragraph 11(3) /11(4) of the Employees' Pension Scheme, 1995 are set aside," according to the ruling.

The court considered the Supreme Court's ruling in EPFO v. Sunil Kumar B., which upheld the 2014 EPS amendments. The Supreme Court had also held that employees who contributed to the PF on actual wages exceeding the statutory ceiling could not be debarred from exercising the higher-pension option solely on that ground, subject to the scheme's conditions.

No. The judgment does not automatically entitle every EPFO member to a higher pension. Employees must meet the applicable eligibility conditions, and the required contributions and other relevant requirements still matter.

The ruling clarifies that an employer's PF trust rules, by themselves, cannot be used to deny an otherwise eligible employee access to the statutory higher-pension option.

data.title: The week in charts: FPI selloff, Reliance bets, Blinkit's expansion plans
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 24 -- From foreign investors continuing to pull money out of Indian equities to unusual leveraged bets on Reliance Industries Ltd, the week saw key developments across markets and business.

Eternal raised its target for Blinkit's dark store expansion, while the government outlined plans to corporatize 11 major ports to speed up decision-making. Meanwhile, Australian pacer Mitchell Starc reached the 450-wicket milestone in men's Test cricket, joining an elite group of bowlers-here is this week's news in numbers.

Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) pulled out Rs.48,056 crore from Indian equities till 23 October, extending the exodus of foreign capital from the market. High crude oil prices, rising US bond yields and a stronger dollar have weighed on investor sentiment.

If October ends with net outflows, it will be the seventh month in 2026 to see foreign investors pull money out of Indian equities. Cumulative net outflows have reached about Rs.3.10 trillion this year, nearly double the Rs.1.66 trillion recorded in 2025.

Last week, finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman flagged the flight of foreign capital towards the US and markets offering greater opportunities in artificial intelligence (AI) as 'a concern'.

Two traders have built large leveraged positions in Reliance Industries Ltd (RIL), a move analysts have described as 'rarest of rare', a Mint report said. Stock exchange data shows that both traders hold positions exceeding 3% each of RIL's marketwide position limit (MWPL).

The unusual bets come ahead of the initial public offering (IPO) of Jio Platforms Ltd, RIL's telecom and digital services subsidiary, in which it owns about 66%. They also come as RIL shares have fallen sharply, hitting a 52-week low on 13 October.

India's most-valued listed company, RIL, could see value unlocked through Jio Platforms' public listing, which would give the subsidiary an independent market valuation. However, the rationale behind the traders' bets remains unclear.

Eternal is stepping up its expansion plans for quick-commerce business Blinkit, raising its target to 3,500 dark stores by March 2027 from the earlier target of 3,000. The company had 2,751 stores as of September 2026, adding 308 during the second quarter.

Eternal's consolidated revenue from operations rose 77.6% year-on-year to Rs.24,138 crore in the September quarter. However, profit margins remained thin, and the company reported a cash outflow of Rs.1,813 crore. Blinkit accounted for 80% of Eternal's revenue, making its expansion central to the company's growth plans.

Eternal remains confident that opening more stores in smaller cities will make business sense. The higher store target also comes as its main rival, Zepto, faces hurdles in raising funds.

7.9%: This is the year-on-year growth in India's core sector output in September, up from 5.9% in August. Iron ore, electricity, coal and refinery products led the growth.

759: Number of H-1B visa registrations filed by Infosys for FY27, down from 8,886 a year earlier, amid tighter US immigration policies. TCS registrations fell to 284 from 5,955 last year.

6.5%: Decline in vehicle registrations during this year's Navratri festival, according to the Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations (Fada). The 2025 festival period had also benefited from GST cuts.

15: Amazon delivery facilities in New York that the e-commerce giant has threatened to close if a proposed bill mandating direct employment of delivery drivers becomes law.

28%: Share of software budgets that large enterprises spend, on average, on vendor upgrades and licensing, leaving less room for investment in AI and innovation, according to a study by software maintenance provider Origina.

The government plans to convert 11 of India's 12 major ports into professionally managed companies with independent boards by 2030. The move aims to speed up decisions on port operations, funding and expansion. Under the current system, administrative processes can slow decisions when cargo patterns change or customers' needs evolve.

Over the past four years, the combined revenue of the 12 major ports has grown at a compounded annual rate of 10.7%. Kamarajar Port near Chennai is the only major port currently run as a company. Under the proposed model, the port company will manage basic infrastructure, while private operators will run terminals and handle cargo under public-private partnership agreements. The new structure is expected to help ports respond more quickly to business needs and facilitate expansion.

Mitchell Starc's 450th Test wicket this week put him among an elite group of 10 bowlers to reach the milestone. The Australian left-arm pacer dismissed South Africa's Wiaan Mulder in the second Test, reaching the landmark in his 109th match. Sri Lankan spinner Muttiah Muralitharan leads the list with 800 wickets in 133 Tests.

However, Starc stands apart for his strike rate, that is, the speed at which he takes wickets. He needs just 46 balls, on average, to claim a wicket-the lowest among the 10 bowlers in the list. That makes him the quickest wicket-taker in the group, though not the most economical. Starc concedes 3.43 runs per over, reflecting the trade-off that comes with his attacking style: he takes wickets quickly but also gives batters more scoring opportunities.

data.title: Infosys shares: Should you buy the IT stock after Q2 results, dividend 2026 announcement? Expert view on what to do
data.description:
Infosys shares, Oct. 24 -- IT major Infosys posted its earnings for the quarter ended September 2026 (Q2 Results) on Friday, October 24. The Bengaluru-based firm delivered year-on-year growth in profit and revenue, announced a sharper-than-expected cut to its full-year growth forecast.

The company lowered its revenue growth guidance for FY27 to 1%-2% from the earlier range of 1.5%-3%, disappointing investors who had anticipated a narrower reduction to 1.5%-2.5%.

Infosys reported consolidated net profit of Rs.7,823 crore for the September quarter, marking a 6.2% increase from Rs.7,364 crore in the corresponding period last year. Consolidated revenue from operations rose 10.2% year-on-year to Rs.49,244 crore from Rs.44,490 crore.

AI-related revenue accounted for 10.5% of total revenue and grew 29% quarter-on-quarter, indicating the increasing contribution of AI-led services to the company's business.

CEO and Managing Director Salil Parekh said Infosys secured large deals worth $5.2 billion during the quarter, including a mega deal valued at more than $2 billion.

However, the company lowered its FY27 revenue growth forecast to 1%-2%, compared with its previous guidance of 1.5%-3%. Infosys had already reduced its full-year forecast in the June quarter, from 1.5%-3.5% to 1.5%-3%, citing macroeconomic uncertainty and its assessment of demand for the remainder of the financial year.

Jayesh Sanghrajka, CFO of Infosys, attributed the latest revision to competitive intensity and customer expectations around productivity. "We are seeing pricing pressures on intense competition and customers asking for higher productivity. That's reflecting in our revised guidance," he said.

"We delivered operating margins of 21.0% in Q2 amidst heightened volatility. Focus on cost and operational efficiency measures, while making the required investments, has led to stable margins," said CFO Jayesh Sanghrajka.

Infosys' board of directors on Friday approved an interim dividend of Rs.26 per share, equivalent to 500% of the stock's face value. Along with the dividend announcement, the company also finalised the record date for identifying eligible shareholders and the timeline for payment.

According to Infosys' filing with the BSE, November 3 has been fixed as the record date to determine shareholders eligible to receive the interim dividend. Investors must hold the company's shares as per the applicable record-date requirements to qualify for the payout. The dividend payment is scheduled to be completed by November 11.

Infosys shares ended 0.3% higher at Rs.1,154.50 on the BSE on Friday, before the company announced its Q2 results after market hours. However, its American depositary receipts (ADRs) fell 6.5% to $12.35 on Friday following the results announcement.

The stock has declined 0.6% over one week but gained 13% over one month and 10% over three months. Over longer periods, it has fallen 7% in six months and 25% in one year.

Infosys is currently around 33% below its 52-week high of Rs.1,727.85, recorded in February 2026. It touched a 52-week low of Rs.980.30 in September 2026.

The recent performance reflects the challenges facing the IT sector, with investors monitoring revenue guidance, client spending and the impact of AI on traditional services.

Expert views on the stock's technical indicators and key support and resistance levels offer further insight into its near-term trajectory.

Jigar S Patel, Senior Manager - Technical Research at Anand Rathi Share and Stock Brokers, said Infosys was struggling near its previous major swing high of Rs.1,193.50. The stock faced selling pressure around this level during the week and closed below it, suggesting that sustained buying interest had yet to emerge at higher prices.

Although the hourly Relative Strength Index (RSI) indicated improving bullish momentum, Patel cautioned that a short-term pullback remained possible. He identified Rs.1,195 as the key resistance level and said a decisive daily close above it would strengthen the bullish outlook and help confirm the formation of a major bottom.

On the downside, Rs.1,050 remains an important support level. Patel said long-term investors could consider accumulating the stock on dips for portfolio allocation, while fresh short-term trading positions should be avoided until a sustained breakout above Rs.1,195 confirms a stronger recovery.

"Overall, long-term investors may consider accumulating the stock on dips for portfolio allocation. However, fresh short-term trading positions are not advisable until a sustained breakout above Rs.1,195 confirms a stronger recovery," Patel added.

For investors, the decision will depend on their investment horizon and risk appetite. While Infosys reported growth in quarterly profit and revenue and secured large deals, its reduced guidance highlights continuing demand and pricing challenges.

The EAAA India Alternatives IPO has a total offer size of Rs.1,200 crore, consisting entirely of an Offer for Sale (OFS), with a price band of Rs.1,585 to Rs.1,665 per share.

Under the SEBI rules, up to 33.33% of the anchor investor portion is reserved for domestic mutual funds. This means that the mutual fund allocation in this IPO exceeded the specified limit.

However, EAAA India Alternatives should not be confused with Edelweiss Mutual Fund. According to its red herring prospectus (RHP), EAAA Alternatives and Edelweiss AMC are "fellow subsidiaries" under their ultimate holding company, Edelweiss Financial Services.

Here are the details of the mutual fund schemes that received the allocations in this IPO anchor book.

Of the 13 schemes, 11 are mutual fund schemes, including active equity and sectoral funds, while two are specialised investment funds (SIFs).

SBI Midcap Fund received the highest allocation, with 2,28,231 shares worth approximately Rs.38 crore, accounting for 10.56% of the anchor investor portion. ICICI Prudential Smallcap Fund received the same number of shares.

The two SIFs are Kotak Infinity Hybrid Long-Short Fund and DynasIF Equity Ex-Top 100 Long Short Fund.

Schemes receiving the allotment will hold EAAA India Alternatives shares in their portfolios on the listing day, which is proposed to be November 2, 2026.

Under the anchor investor lock-in rules, 50% of the allotted anchor shares are locked in for 30 days from the allotment date, while the remaining 50% are locked in for 90 days. During the respective lock-in periods, the shares cannot be sold or transferred to another scheme.

After the lock-in expires, fund managers of active schemes can decide whether to retain, sell, or add to their holdings. They may also purchase additional shares from the listing day.

According to its RHP, EAAA India Alternatives is one of India's leading alternative investment platforms, incorporated in May 2008. Its assets under management stood around Rs.95,345 crore as of June 30, 2026.

Its managed funds have 11,009 client relationships across India and overseas, including institutional investors, ultra-high-net-worth individuals (UHNIs), high-net-worth individuals (HNIs) and family offices.

Its key business verticals are real assets and private credit. The real assets vertical had eight active funds and two InvITs, while the private credit vertical manages 16 active funds. The company also offers portfolio management services (PMS) and other services.

For mutual fund investors, the allotment provides indirect exposure to EAAA India Alternatives through the schemes they hold. However, whether a scheme retains or sells the shares after listing will depend on its fund manager's investment decisions and the scheme's mandate.

data.title: Gold rates in Chennai city crash this week: Can yellow metal rebound ahead of Diwali - Key levels to watch in future?
data.description:
Gold price outlook, Oct. 24 -- Gold prices witnessed a sharp sell-off this week as rising crude oil prices, a stronger US dollar and elevated US Treasury yields weighed on bullion. Renewed inflation concerns and expectations of tighter US monetary policy further pressured precious metals, leading to declines in both MCX futures and retail gold prices in Chennai.

Over the week, MCX gold futures fell around 3.50%, with heavy selling pulling prices down from their previous highs. In Chennai, retail gold prices dropped 3.85%. The price of 24K gold fell by Rs.5,560 per 10 grams, from Rs.1,48,190 to Rs.1,42,480.

On Friday alone, MCX gold futures declined 0.92%, falling Rs.1,315 to settle at around Rs.1,41,994 per 10 grams.

In Chennai, retail gold prices dropped 1.32% on Friday. The price of 24K gold fell by Rs.190 per gram to Rs.14,248, while 22K jewellery gold declined by Rs.175 per gram to Rs.13,060.

Globally as well, gold prices have come under intense pressure as surging crude oil prices, Bullion fell to a three-month low on Friday and was heading for its steepest weekly decline in more than four months, putting the psychologically important $4,000-an-ounce mark in focus ahead of the US Federal Reserve's October 27-28 policy meeting.

Gold has declined around 4% this week, marking its weakest weekly performance since June.

Rising energy prices have emerged as a major headwind for bullion. Brent crude touched a more than five-month high after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia heightened concerns over disruptions to global energy supplies. Higher oil prices can fuel inflation, potentially forcing central banks to maintain restrictive monetary policies for longer.

Although traders largely expect the Federal Reserve to leave interest rates unchanged at its October 27-28 meeting, stronger-than-expected US consumer and producer inflation data have strengthened expectations of possible monetary tightening later this year. Markets are also watching next week's personal consumption expenditures (PCE) inflation data, the Fed's preferred measure of inflation.

Saish Sawant, Research Analyst-Commodities at Emkay Global Financial Services, said gold's decline had been amplified by investors selling liquid assets to meet margin calls following a sharp correction in US equities.

"Gold is heading for its steepest weekly decline in four months, down over 3.5% and holding above $4,000/oz after briefly slipping below that level for the first time since 29 July. Cross-asset deleveraging has driven the move, as a sharp correction in US equities pushed investors to sell liquid holdings such as gold to meet margin calls," Sawant said.

The US dollar and Treasury yields have also influenced bullion prices. While both have eased this week, the dollar index remained near 101.5, close to a three-week low, and the 10-year US Treasury yield fell to a one-month low amid safe-haven demand for government bonds. Sawant noted that gold had fallen approximately 20% from its level at the onset of the US-Iran conflict in late February.

The near-term technical outlook remains weak, with gold struggling around the $4,000-an-ounce threshold. Renisha Chainani, Chief Research Officer at Augmont, said a sustained move below this level could open the door to further declines towards $3,950, equivalent to approximately Rs.1,40,000, from around Rs.1,42,000 at the $4,000 level.

Over the medium term, however, Chainani expects gold and silver to attempt to establish a base. She identified $3,950-$4,000 as a potential support and accumulation zone for gold, while silver could find support around $50-$55.

Chainani expects the precious metal to hold these levels and potentially rebound 10-15% over the coming weeks. For gold's broader uptrend to resume, she said prices would need to sustain above $4,200 an ounce.

Meanwhile, Sawant maintained a bearish near-term view, warning that continued selling could push gold towards the previous swing low of $3,940. He added that changing expectations around artificial intelligence-led growth could eventually provide some support by influencing interest-rate expectations, once the current wave of liquidation subsides.

"The near-term trend remains bearish, and persistent selling risks a retest of the $3,940 swing low. Doubts over AI-led growth are already trimming rate expectations, which should provide support over time once the liquidation fades," Sawant said.

Despite the correction in prices, jewellery demand could remain resilient during the festive season. Kaushlendra Sinha, CEO of IAGES, said consumers continued to regard gold as a store of value and could view softer prices as an opportunity to buy.

"This festive season, gold demand is expected to remain strong as consumers continue to view gold as a trusted store of value. While Gold prices which seems to have softened up from the highs, we see this as an opportunity and confidence in gold continues to hold firm," Sinha said.

Sinha added that buyers were increasingly prioritising purity, ethical sourcing and transparency alongside design and value. Lightweight jewellery and old-gold exchange programmes were also gaining traction as consumer preferences evolved.

data.title: German traveller reveals 10 things she wishes she knew before travelling to India as a solo traveller
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 24 -- The video of a German travel vlogger has gone viral on social media, in which she speaks about things that she wishes she had known before visiting India. The Instagram user paulahnck posted the video with a caption reading "For my western girlies that wanna go to India."

In the video, she shared 10 tips for solo female travellers in India.

Tuk-tuks, buses, trains. They're cheap and take you anywhere.

"You even have women-only seats and sleeper sections on many trains and buses. I prefer buses," she noted.

She also pointed out that travelers can use apps like Rapido, Uber, and RedBus to travel from one place to another.

"Mobile data in India is insanely cheap. I paid 6€ for 4 GB a day for a month. Just remember to bring your passport when buying a SIM card. I recommend Airtel," she said.

"The website is a pain. Do it on a laptop and give yourself enough time. For those planning to return to India, the woman suggested considering a one-year visa to avoid the hassle of applying again soon," she noted.

"If you're from Europe, you'll probably underestimate them. Either book a flight or take overnight buses/trains to save time", she said, adding that "I personally preferred buses and booked almost everything through RedBus."

"If you're feeling sick, the supermarket is far away, or no one can bring you something: you can order anything in India. everything. Apps: Blinkit/Zomato," she wrote.

"It might feel uncomfortable at first, but most of the time it's simply curiosity, not rudeness. You get used to it," she noted.

"I seriously JUST had good experiences," she added.

She also rejected the claim that Indian food was unsafe, while admitting that it was her personal experience.

"I can only speak from my own experience, but I never had any stomach problems. I ate street food, drank chai from roadside stands, and tried everything," she said.

According to her, the Indian head wobble can be confusing, but you'll figure it out eventually.

"It's not the same as a Western nod, and it can be surprisingly hard to tell whether someone means 'yes, okay, or, no'," she wrote.

"Unlike Southeast Asia, Indian hostels have a lot of locals too, she noted, adding that "If that makes you uncomfortable, book a private room or a female-only dorm."

"Even learning the basics can change your experience of India. It helps you understand temples, festivals, rituals, and daily life on a deeper level, even if you're not religious," she said.

data.title: Goldman Sachs Ola Electric Downgrade: Why stock rating changed to sell; 23% downside seen - New target price, rationale
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 24 -- Goldman Sachs Ola Electric downgrade: Goldman Sachs has turned bearish on Ola Electric Mobility, cutting its rating to Sell and reducing its price target sharply, as mounting concerns over cash flow, funding requirements and operational challenges cloud the electric two-wheeler maker's recovery prospects. The global investment bank has warned that the company faces a difficult path towards generating positive free cash flow, with high interest costs and substantial capital expenditure requirements adding to the pressure.

Goldman Sachs lowered its target price to Rs.23 from Rs.39.28, implying a downside of 23% from Ola Electric's previous closing price of Rs.29.93. The brokerage also reduced its revenue estimates for FY27 to FY29 by up to 10%, citing a tougher market-share environment and expectations of prolonged operating losses.

Goldman Sachs' downgrade reflects growing concerns over Ola Electric's growth prospects, financial sustainability and ability to navigate intensifying competition in the electric two-wheeler market.

According to Goldman Sachs, Ola Electric would need a substantial acceleration in revenue to cover its capital expenditure and interest servicing requirements. Revenue during FY28 to FY30 would need to reach 3.6 times to 7.1 times FY26 levels to meet these obligations, it highlighted.

The scale of the challenge is underscored by the company's recent performance. Ola Electric's revenue in FY26 was 55% lower than its FY24 level, making the growth required over the coming years particularly demanding.

Moreover, the brokerage expects operating losses, elevated interest expenses and investments across the electric two-wheeler (E2W) and battery-cell businesses to complicate efforts to generate positive free cash flow. Its revised revenue estimates reflect the increasingly challenging competitive environment compared with other players in the two-wheeler industry.

Goldman Sachs also flagged potential operational headwinds following the recent departure of the head of Ola Electric's battery business. The leadership change raises concerns about the execution of its battery-cell strategy at a time when the company needs to improve operational efficiency and manage its funding requirements.

Despite its cautious assessment, Goldman Sachs identified several factors that could support a recovery. A turnaround in the electric two-wheeler business following the company's shift towards a dealer-led sales and service model could help restore brand sentiment.

Faster customer acquisition for its in-house battery cells and improved profitability in the cell business would also be important. The brokerage said progress on these fronts could help address concerns over the company's ability to scale its operations while improving financial performance.

However, the need to invest in both electric scooters and battery manufacturing, alongside high interest costs, remains a significant hurdle. The company will need to demonstrate that it can improve sales, strengthen profitability and generate sufficient cash to fund its operations without placing additional pressure on its balance sheet.

Earlier this month, Ola Electric finalised the terms of its Rs.1,000-crore rights issue at Rs.27 per share, a 26% discount to its market value at the time. The company will issue 37.03 crore partly paid-up shares. The offer opened on Thursday and will close on October 30, while shareholders can sell or transfer their rights entitlements in the market until October 26.

The fundraising comes just three months after Ola Electric raised Rs.780 crore through a qualified institutional placement (QIP) in June, against an initial plan to raise Rs.500 crore. In the same month, rival Ather Energy approved plans to raise up to Rs.2,500 crore through a QIP and other equity-linked instruments.

Ola Electric narrowed its net loss to Rs.336 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs.428 crore a year earlier, although revenue from operations declined 45% year-on-year to Rs.455 crore from Rs.828 crore. Revenue nevertheless increased 72% from Rs.265 crore in Q4 FY26.

The Bhavish Aggarwal-led company said the April-June quarter was its first full quarter after the FY26 reset, during which it streamlined operations, tightened execution and reduced its operating cost base. Orders increased to 44,071 units from 22,522 units in the previous quarter, while deliveries rose to 39,192 units from 20,256 units.

However, Vahan vehicle registration data, a proxy for sales, showed that Ola Electric sold 12,894 electric two-wheelers in September, translating into a 6.5% market share, down from 7.6% in August.

Ola Electric shares closed 6.3% lower at Rs.29.93 on the BSE in the previous trading session. The stock has declined more than 14% over the past week, 28% over one month, 19% over three months and 44% over one year.

The shares are currently 44% below their 52-week high of Rs.53.47, recorded in October 2025. The stock touched its 52-week low of Rs.20.83 in March 2026.

Goldman Sachs' downgrade adds to the pressure on the stock, with the brokerage highlighting the need for stronger revenue growth, improved battery-cell execution and a clearer path to positive free cash flow. The company's ability to revive sales while controlling costs and funding requirements will remain crucial to its recovery.

Rs. 22,600) and go up to 49,500 yen (around Rs. 30,000).

data.title: Ukraine seeks Starlink alternative after Musk's satellite disruptions: What Nokia and ICEYE are building?
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 24 -- Days after Ukraine reported restrictions on its access to Starlink and Starshield satellite internet services provided by US billionaire Elon Musk's SpaceX, causing fast-moving drones to disconnect, Kyiv is now partnering with the Finnish companies Nokia and ICEYE to develop new defence and satellite communications capabilities.

In a press release on Thursday (local time), Nokia announced that the two companies had signed a Letter of Intent (LoI) with Ukraine's defence ministry to explore cooperation in space. The partnership aims to support Kyiv's defence capabilities, particularly by building sovereign satellite communications. According to reports, the goal is to develop a secure satellite communications system of Kyiv's own.

Earlier this month, the two Finnish companies also announced a collaboration to create secure, sovereign and high-performance broadband satellite communications systems in low Earth orbit (LEO) for governments, Nokia said. These systems would support missions ranging from defence and border security to emergency services and disaster response. The satellite communications systems will give nations ownership and control of the satellites, ground segment and terminals.

According to Space.com, ICEYE is already aiding Kyiv's defence effort. ICEYE and its US subsidiary jointly run a network of Earth-observation satellites in low Earth orbit, using synthetic aperture radar to monitor the planet. Ukraine draws on imagery from the constellation to support intelligence gathering and operational planning.

The partnership was announced during the Finnish prime minister's visit to Ukraine. Commenting on the collaboration, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said, "Modern warfare has proven that reliable communications are a matter of national security. We must all rely on capabilities that we can control.

The Letter of Intent between the Ministry of Defense, ICEYE, and Nokia is an important step in this direction. I thank Finland and the Prime Minister of Finland for their consistent support. We value partners who not only help Ukraine, but also work with us to build Europe's long-term security."

Rafal Modrzewski, CEO and co-founder of ICEYE, said, "Ukraine needs secure, sovereign and high-performance satellite communications systems that it controls. We have a proven track record of delivering sovereign missions at speed to help build that capability. ICEYE has proudly supported Ukraine since 2022, and we remain it to continuing that support today."

Separately, Zelenskyy has also announced a partnership with Norway to jointly develop air defence and communications systems that could serve as an alternative to Starshield.

The push for satellite communications under Ukrainian control comes amid growing concerns over Kyiv's reliance on SpaceX, after recent service restrictions disrupted connections on fast-moving drones.

The development comes at a time when Kyiv has been struggling to intercept and launch drones after Musk's SpaceX reportedly restricted the country's access to Starshield, the military version of the system. According to Zelenskyy, connection speeds on Starlink, a service Ukraine used for some military activities, including defence against Russian missile attacks, had been reduced.

Both US President Donald Trump and Musk have denied responsibility for the unannounced restrictions, which Kyiv first reported on 14 October and said remained in place as of Friday (local time). Trump told reporters on Friday that he would call the billionaire to have the restrictions lifted.

Separately, the Financial Times reported earlier this week that four of Europe's major telecom groups, Deutsche Telekom, Orange, Telefónica and Vodafone, are also considering satellite mobile services of their own to lessen reliance on providers outside the European Union and compete with Musk's Starlink.

data.title: Merz calls for unity as he warns of threats facing Germany
data.description:
Key points:
  • Merz urges unity amid coalition strains after election setbacks
  • Warns of extremism, accuses Russia of destabilisation
  • Urges economic reforms, rejects cooperation with far-right AfD

Chancellor Friedrich Merz called for unity in his struggling coalition on Saturday, saying Germany faced growing threats from political extremists and what he described as daily Russian efforts to destabilise the country.

Speaking at a conference of the Christian Social Union (CSU), the Bavarian sister party of his conservative Christian Democrats (CDU), Merz said Germany faced "extraordinarily serious challenges".

"How do we safeguard our freedom and our security in Europe, in the face of growing threats from extremists within and foreign powers from without?" he said, adding that Russia was seeking "to destabilise Germany on a daily basis".

Relations between Berlin and Moscow have fallen to their lowest level since the Cold War following Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine but Russia rejects accusations that it is conducting a hybrid campaign against Germany and other European countries.

Merz's comments follow weeks of tension with the ruling coalition after heavy regional election defeats in eastern Germany, where the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) came first in two states and the far-left Left Party topped the poll in Berlin.

Merz's approval ratings have fallen to record lows, while tensions have surfaced both between the coalition partners and between the CDU and CSU.

The two conservative sister parties have a long history of disagreements but have generally managed to overcome them.

On Saturday, delegates broke into loud applause when Merz mentioned Ilse Aigner, the CSU politician the party has proposed as successor to German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier, who is due to step down next year.

The CDU has so far stopped short of endorsing Aigner, and party sources say it has not abandoned hopes of putting forward its own candidate for the largely ceremonial post of head of state.

Merz, who entered the conference hall to a Bavarian brass band playing "The Eye of the Tiger", praised CSU ministers in the government and paid tribute to CSU leader Markus Soeder.

But he repeated his rejection of calls from some conservatives to seek ways of cooperating with the AfD, which leads national opinion polls, saying any politician who voted with the party "has no place in our Union".

He also urged the Social Democrats (SPD) and Greens not to form a coalition in Berlin with the Left Party, which he accused of tolerating antisemitism within its ranks. The Left Party denies any systemic antisemitism in the party.

Merz said rapid reforms to Germany's pension, tax and welfare systems were essential to revive the economy and restore confidence in public institutions.

data.title: ESMO 2026: NUBEQA® (darolutamide) Plus ADT and Radiation Therapy Reduces Risk of Metastasis or Death by 58% in Prostate Cancer Patients at High Risk of Recurrence
data.description:
New late-breaking data to be presented today by the Australian and New Zealand Urogenital and Prostate (ANZUP) Clinical Trials Group at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress 2026 will show that adding Bayer’s androgen receptor inhibitor (ARi), NUBEQA® (darolutamide), to standard-of-care androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) and locoregional radiation therapy (RT), improves metastasis-free survival based on conventional imaging (MFS-CI) in prostate cancer patients with high risk of recurrence compared to placebo. These data will be presented at Presidential Symposium I at the ESMO Congress 2026 (LBA4, Saturday, October 24, at 16:30 CEST/10:30 am ET).

NUBEQA is indicated in the U.S. for the treatment of adult patients with metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer (mCSPC) both with and without docetaxel, and for the treatment of adult patients with non-metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (nmCRPC).1

At a median follow-up of 3.8 years, the interim analysis demonstrated a statistically significant 58% reduction in the risk of metastasis or death with NUBEQA plus ADT and RT compared with placebo plus ADT and RT (hazard ratio [HR] 0.42; 95% CI: 0.27–0.66; p=0.0001).2 The 4-year metastasis-free survival rate was 95% for patients receiving NUBEQA compared with 88% for those receiving placebo.2

“Prostate cancer patients at a high risk of relapse face a considerable risk of recurrence and metastatic spread, making early, effective intervention vital,” said Dr. Tamim Niazi, Associate Professor of Oncology at McGill University, Radiation Oncologist at the Jewish General Hospital in Montreal, Canada, and Co-Lead Investigator of the study. “The improvement in metastasis-free survival seen in interim results from the DASL-HiCaP trial highlights the potential of adding darolutamide to standard androgen deprivation therapy and radiation therapy to help prevent or delay disease progression in patients who are at high risk of progression despite receiving primary curative therapy.”

Secondary endpoints showed NUBEQA was associated with a 53% reduction in the risk of prostate-specific antigen progression or death (PSA-PFS; HR 0.47; 95% CI: 0.33–0.67), and a 4-year PSA-PFS rate of 91% versus 83% with placebo.2 Prostate cancer-specific survival (PCSS) and overall survival (OS) hazard ratios were 0.58 (95% CI: 0.17–1.97; 99% vs 99% at 4 years) and 0.88 (95% CI: 0.49–1.59; 97% vs 95% at 4 years), respectively, with follow-up ongoing.2

The safety profile of NUBEQA was consistent with previous studies. The proportions of patients experiencing Grade ≥2 adverse events of special interest for NUBEQA versus placebo were: fatigue/asthenia (14% vs 10%), hypertension (7% vs 9%), fractures (2% vs 3%), and cardiac events (3% vs 3%). Any Grade ≥3 adverse event occurred in 43% of patients in the NUBEQA group versus 36% in the placebo group.2

“These new data underscore the potential of darolutamide to improve outcomes for patients in the early prostate cancer setting, adding to the broad body of evidence helping to support its use across different stages of the disease,” said Christine Roth, Executive Vice President, Global Product Strategy and Commercialization at Bayer’s Pharmaceuticals Division. “Bayer is proud to support research by ANZUP, the Sydney Clinical Trials Centre, Canadian Cancer Trials Group, and international partners, for men with prostate cancer.”

About the DASL-HiCaP trial (ANZUP1801)

The DASL-HiCaP trial is an investigator-initiated, randomized, placebo-controlled, Phase III trial (NCT04136353) evaluating NUBEQA added to standard-of-care ADT and locoregional radiation therapy in prostate cancer patients at high risk of recurrence.

DASL-HiCaP was conducted in collaboration with the University of Sydney and ANZUP Clinical Trials Group and is the fourth Phase III trial for darolutamide to be presented at a prestigious international conference.

A total of 1,106 participants across Australia, New Zealand, Canada, the United States, Ireland and the United Kingdom were randomized 1:1 to receive NUBEQA (600 mg twice daily) or matching placebo for 96 weeks, combined with an LHRH analog for 96 weeks and RT to the prostate/prostate bed and pelvic lymph nodes.

The primary endpoint was metastasis-free survival based on conventional imaging (MFS-CI). Secondary endpoints included prostate-specific antigen progression free survival (PSA-PFS), prostate cancer-specific survival (PCSS), and overall survival (OS). The protocol specified an interim analysis after 87 MFS-CI events; follow-up is ongoing to evaluate long-term overall survival.

About NUBEQA® (darolutamide)1

NUBEQA® (darolutamide) is an androgen receptor inhibitor (ARi) with a distinct chemical structure that competitively inhibits androgen binding, AR nuclear translocation, and AR-mediated transcription.

NUBEQA was developed jointly by Bayer and Orion Corporation, a globally operating Finnish pharmaceutical company.

NUBEQA is an androgen receptor inhibitor indicated for the treatment of adult patients with:

  • Non-metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (nmCRPC)

  • Metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer (mCSPC)

  • Metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer (mCSPC) in combination with docetaxel

IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION

Warnings & Precautions

Ischemic Heart Disease – Ischemic heart disease, including fatal cases, occurred in patients receiving NUBEQA.

In a pooled analysis of ARAMIS and ARANOTE, ischemic heart disease occurred in 3.4% of patients receiving NUBEQA and 2.2% receiving placebo, including Grade 3-4 events in 1.4% and 0.3%, respectively. Ischemic events led to death in 0.4% of patients receiving NUBEQA and 0.4% receiving placebo.

In ARASENS, ischemic heart disease occurred in 3.2% of patients receiving NUBEQA with docetaxel and 2% receiving placebo with docetaxel, including Grade 3-4 events in 1.3% and 1.1%, respectively. Ischemic events led to death in 0.3% of patients receiving NUBEQA with docetaxel and 0% receiving placebo with docetaxel.

Monitor for signs and symptoms of ischemic heart disease. Optimize management of cardiovascular risk factors, such as hypertension, diabetes, or dyslipidemia. Discontinue NUBEQA for Grade 3-4 ischemic heart disease.

Seizure – Seizure occurred in patients receiving NUBEQA.

In a pooled analysis of ARAMIS and ARANOTE, Grade 1-3 seizure occurred in 0.2% of patients receiving NUBEQA. Seizure occurred from 261 to 665 days after initiation of NUBEQA.

In ARASENS, seizure occurred in 0.8% of patients receiving NUBEQA with docetaxel, including two Grade 3 events. Seizure occurred from 38 to 1754 days after initiation of NUBEQA.

It is unknown whether anti-epileptic medications will prevent seizures with NUBEQA. Advise patients of the risk of developing a seizure while receiving NUBEQA and of engaging in any activity where sudden loss of consciousness could cause harm to themselves or others. Consider discontinuation of NUBEQA in patients who develop a seizure during treatment.

Embryo-Fetal Toxicity – The safety and efficacy of NUBEQA have not been established in females. NUBEQA can cause fetal harm and loss of pregnancy. Advise males with female partners of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during treatment with NUBEQA and for 1 week after the last dose.

Adverse Reactions

In ARAMIS, serious adverse reactions occurred in 25% of patients receiving NUBEQA and in 20% of patients receiving placebo. Serious adverse reactions in ≥1% of patients who received NUBEQA included urinary retention, pneumonia, and hematuria. Fatal adverse reactions occurred in 3.9% of patients receiving NUBEQA and 3.2% of patients receiving placebo. Fatal adverse reactions that occurred in ≥2 patients who received NUBEQA included death (0.4%), cardiac failure (0.3%), cardiac arrest (0.2%), general physical health deterioration (0.2%), and pulmonary embolism (0.2%). The most common (>2% with a ≥2% increase compared to placebo) adverse reactions, including laboratory test abnormalities, were increased AST (23%), decreased neutrophil count (20%), fatigue (16%), increased bilirubin (16%), pain in extremity (6%), and rash (4%). Clinically relevant adverse reactions occurring in 2% or more of patients treated with NUBEQA included ischemic heart disease (4%) and heart failure (2.1%).

In ARANOTE, serious adverse reactions occurred in 24% of patients receiving NUBEQA. Serious adverse reactions in ≥1% of patients who received NUBEQA included pneumonia (2%), urinary tract infection (1.8%), musculoskeletal pain (1.6%), hemorrhage (1.6%), arrhythmias (1.3%), and spinal cord compression (1.1%). Fatal adverse reactions occurred in 4.7% of patients receiving NUBEQA and those that occurred in ≥2 patients included sepsis (1.1%), craniocerebral injury (0.4%), and myocardial infarction (0.4%). The most common (≥10% with a ≥2% increase compared to placebo) adverse reaction is urinary tract infection (12%). The most common laboratory test abnormalities (≥15% with a ≥5% increase over placebo) are increased AST (32%), increased ALT (28%), increased bilirubin (17%), and decreased neutrophil count (16%). Clinically relevant adverse reactions in <10% of patients who received NUBEQA included arrhythmia (8.8%), pneumonia (3.6%), and myocardial infarction (0.7%).

In ARASENS, serious adverse reactions occurred in 45% of patients receiving NUBEQA with docetaxel. Serious adverse reactions in ≥2% of patients who received NUBEQA with docetaxel included febrile neutropenia (6%), neutrophil count decreased (2.8%), musculoskeletal pain (2.6%) and pneumonia (2.6%). Fatal adverse reactions occurred in 4% of patients receiving NUBEQA with docetaxel. Fatal adverse reactions in ≥2 patients who received NUBEQA included COVID-19/COVID-19 pneumonia (0.8%), myocardial infarction (0.3%), and sudden death (0.3%). The most common (≥10% with a ≥2% increase over placebo with docetaxel) adverse reactions are constipation (23%), rash (20%), decreased appetite (19%), hemorrhage (18%), increased weight (18%), and hypertension (14%). The most common laboratory test abnormalities (≥30%) are anemia (72%), hyperglycemia (57%), decreased lymphocyte count (52%), decreased neutrophil count (49%), increased AST (40%), increased ALT (37%), and hypocalcemia (31%). Clinically relevant adverse reactions in <10% of patients who received NUBEQA with docetaxel included fractures (8%), ischemic heart disease (3.2%), seizures (0.6%), and drug-induced liver injury (0.3%).

Drug Interactions

Effect of Other Drugs on NUBEQA – Concomitant use of NUBEQA with a combined P-gp and strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducer decreases darolutamide exposure which may decrease NUBEQA activity. Avoid concomitant use of NUBEQA with combined P-gp and strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers.

Concomitant use of NUBEQA with a combined P-gp and strong CYP3A4 inhibitor increases darolutamide exposure which may increase the risk of NUBEQA adverse reactions. Monitor patients more frequently for NUBEQA adverse reactions and modify NUBEQA dosage as needed.

Effects of NUBEQA on Other Drugs – NUBEQA is an inhibitor of BCRP transporter. Concomitant use of NUBEQA increases the AUC and Cmax of BCRP substrates, which may increase the risk of BCRP substrate-related toxicities. Avoid concomitant use with drugs that are BCRP substrates where possible. If used together, monitor patients more frequently for adverse reactions, and consider dose reduction of the BCRP substrate drug.

NUBEQA is an inhibitor of OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 transporters. Concomitant use of NUBEQA may increase the plasma concentrations of OATP1B1 or OATP1B3 substrates. Monitor patients more frequently for adverse reactions of these drugs and consider dose reduction while patients are taking NUBEQA.

Review the Prescribing Information of drugs that are BCRP, OATP1B1, and OATP1B3 substrates when used concomitantly with NUBEQA.

For important risk and use information about NUBEQA, please see the accompanying full Prescribing Information.

Please see the full Prescribing Information.

data.title: Defensive Plays Are Gaining Steam. 5 Heavily Shorted Names Could Pop. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Evie Liu

Some of the market's most beaten-down consumer stocks have been making a comeback — and investors betting against them could provide additional fuel for the rally.

Consumer-staples stocks surged in October as investors shifted money away from technology companies amid concerns about lofty valuations and slowing economic growth. The Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR exchange-traded fund has gained nearly 10% as of Friday's close, reversing a 4.5% decline in September.

Several rebounding companies have seen unusually high short interest. Short sellers borrow and sell shares, hoping to buy them back later at lower prices and pocket the difference. But when a heavily-shorted stock rises sharply, those investors can face mounting losses and may rush to buy shares to close their positions — which could add to demand and push prices even higher.

Flowers Foods, the maker of Nature's Own and Dave's Killer Bread, is one potential candidate. As of Sept. 30, nearly 23% of its publicly traded shares were sold short, according to FactSet. The stock has gained nearly 11% in October through Friday.

Boston Beer, the maker of Samuel Adams and Twisted Tea, also stands out. About 21% of its float was sold short at September's end. Shares have rallied 23% this month through Friday.

There are reasons for caution: Both companies are struggling with declining revenue, raising doubts about whether their stock rallies can last.

In the latest quarter, Flowers Foods reported a 4% revenue decline year over year and lowered its annual earnings forecast. Likewise, Boston Beer's revenue fell 3.2% as its sales volume shrunk nearly 5% from a year ago.

Pet food company Freshpet might be a better bet. Its revenue grew 15.5% year over year in the latest quarter, driven almost entirely by higher sales volumes as the company attracted more customers and expanded distribution.

Still, 17% of its publicly traded shares were sold short by the end of September as investors worried about slowing growth and intensifying competition. Its shares have climbed 11% this month through Friday, potentially putting pressure on short sellers to close their positions if the rally continues.

Freshpet has a days-to-cover ratio — days needed to buy back all the shares sold short at a stock's average daily trading volume — of 7.9 days, compared with 5.3 for Flowers Foods and 5.1 for Boston Beer. That suggests short sellers could face greater difficulty exiting their positions quickly if Freshpet shares surge.

Sprouts Farmers Market and Vital Farms also have relatively high short interest, with about 14% and 24% of their respective floats sold short by the end of September. Both stocks rallied Thursday, although they have been largely flat compared with the beginning of the month.

High short interest, however, doesn't guarantee a squeeze. Some bearish bets reflect genuine business challenges, and short sellers may be willing to withstand temporary losses.

And the defensive rally itself remains fragile. The consumer-staples ETF fell about 2% on Friday, reversing part of its sharp advance on Thursday. Flowers Foods and Freshpet each dropped more than 4%, while Sprouts Farmers Market fell 3.8% and Vital Farms lost 2.9%. Boston Beer bucked the trend, gaining 3.6% following its earnings report on Thursday.

Without sustained buying pressure, short sellers have less incentive to exit. Investors will get another clue on Monday, when updated short-interest figures from Finra become available. The report will show positions as of Oct. 15, revealing whether bearish investors reduced their bets during the staples rally — or continued adding to them.

data.title: Bitcoin Core Speeds Up Bug Fixes As AI Changes Disclosure Rules
data.description:
TL;DR: Bitcoin Core has adopted faster fixes and disclosure for vulnerabilities that are easy to rediscover, including with AI. Longer embargoes remain available for other security flaws.

Bitcoin Core is changing the timetable for dealing with security flaws that an attacker can uncover with little effort. The practical question is whether waiting to explain a bug still protects users when software can rediscover it almost immediately.

A policy update merged on October 22 creates a faster route for these cases. Developer Antoine Poinsot argued that large language models have made some problems easier to find, including by identifying fixes that were intended to attract little attention.

That creates a difficult choice for the people maintaining Bitcoin software: withholding details can buy upgrade time, but delaying a usable patch can also leave operators exposed.

Faster Releases For Easily Rediscovered Flaws

The updated disclosure policy allows developers to classify a reported vulnerability as easily discoverable. A simple AI prompt is one example; the category also covers problems found with minimal effort through other means.

For those vulnerabilities, maintainers plan to issue a fix for each supported major version as soon as possible, accompanied by a security advisory. These cases bypass the usual embargo linked to severity.

The distinction matters for an exchange or payment business running its own node. A point release can deliver a targeted repair without waiting for the next major software version. An advisory also helps the operator judge whether its particular configuration is affected.

Other disclosure rules remain. Low-severity issues normally become public two weeks after a major release containing the fix. Medium- and high-severity issues generally wait until two weeks after the last affected version reaches the end of its support life. Critical vulnerabilities still require individual handling.

Less Secrecy Also Means Less Testing Time

The discussion accompanying the change makes clear that speed has a cost. Poinsot noted that accelerated mitigations will spend less time in development branches before reaching users. Developers therefore have to weigh the risk of exposing a flaw against the risk of introducing a faulty repair.

For businesses providing custody, the operational lesson is that patch readiness belongs alongside key security. Maintaining a current inventory of software versions, understanding which services depend on them and having a controlled upgrade process can make a short notice period easier to manage.

The announcement itself does not identify a new attack on the Bitcoin network. It changes how a defined category of software problem will be handled. Readers should therefore distinguish a revised security process from evidence that coins have been stolen or consensus rules have failed.

Its significance is narrower and more practical: when attackers can cheaply rediscover a weakness, keeping users on unfixed software becomes harder to justify. The response shifts toward getting a repair into their hands sooner, while making the remaining trade-offs visible.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

data.title: AI fever ignites a boom in thematic ETFs as fund managers hunt for their next big hit
data.description:
By Christine Idzelis

It's been a rocky October for the AI trade, putting a dent in big gains so far this year

Robotics ETFs are increasingly coming to the stock market, with AI being a dominant investing theme in 2026.

The runaway success of the artificial-intelligence trade has left investors hungry for the next big market theme. Wall Street fund managers are happily obliging with a flurry of new targeted products, helping investors invest in everything from the rise of robotics to the incipient space economy.

Thematic ETFs are booming in 2026, as asset managers have launched new products at a breakneck pace. The popularity of funds like the Roundhill Memory ETF DRAM, which invests in memory stocks as a subsector of technology and quickly gained traction because they're an important part of the AI trade, has inspired something of a gold rush in the space, as fund companies cast about for the next big hit.

Niche subdivisions of the AI theme have proved particularly popular, as fund managers have launched products tied to everything from AI lab ecosystems to shares of optical companies expected to benefit from the ongoing AI investment boom. Cybersecurity, robotics and defense have been other popular themes.

"AI is the dominant theme," said Bryan Armour, director of ETF and semiliquid fund research at Morningstar, in a phone interview. "What we're seeing in 2026 is product development that refines some of those exposures," he said, from AI Labs to robotics including humanoids.

So far, 73 thematic ETFs have launched this year in the U.S., an 87% increase from the 39 launches seen in 2025, according to data from Morningstar. But the boom in new products is also dredging up some uncomfortable memories: The previous peak for thematic ETF launches arrived in 2021, as the COVID-era market mania was reaching its crescendo.

 
Thematic ETF launches are surging in 2026

2020                                          49 
2021                                          90 
2022                                          59
